title: Kam AI: Private Offline AI
shortDescription: Private AI on your phone. No account, no cloud, no subscription, no tracking.
fullDescription:
Kam AI runs on your phone. You download a model once, and after that everything happens on the device: what you ask, what it answers, and anything you save. Nothing is uploaded. Put the phone in airplane mode and you can still chat.

It thinks with you, not for you. That is what the four modes are for, and it
is why one of them refuses to hand you ideas at all.

Logic Partner takes the other side. Describe a plan or an argument and it looks for what is weak in it, asks the question you have been avoiding, and says where the reasoning does not hold. It concedes when you are right, and it does not fold just because you pushed back. Most assistants agree with you by default. This one is built not to.

General handles ordinary questions. Brainstorm refuses to hand you ideas and pulls your own out of you instead, one question at a time. Workbench takes text you paste in and tightens, rewrites or reorganizes it.

Also inside: voice, so you can talk instead of typing, transcribed on the phone. Projects, which keep related chats under instructions they all follow. Memory of the durable things, all of it visible and deletable. Bookmarks for anything worth checking later. Search across your chats, projects and bookmarks. And Discover, offline packs of short readings to pull one from and discuss.

How fast it is. Answers take a few seconds, and the first one after installing takes longest while the model loads. That wait is your phone doing the work a data centre would otherwise do with your words, which is the same reason nothing you type leaves the device. It is slower again when the phone is warm.

What it is not good at. A model small enough to fit on a phone knows less than the large ones in data centers, and it will get obscure facts wrong, because small models guess more. Anything factual is worth checking, which is what the bookmarks are for. It cannot make images. Without a connection it knows nothing about recent events. And it is better at working with text you give it than at writing long polished documents from nothing.

The modes also ask different amounts of the model. General and Workbench are the forgiving ones. Logic Partner and Brainstorm ask more, because holding an argument or running a session means keeping track of what you said several turns ago, and a smaller model does that less reliably. If those modes are why you are here and your phone has the memory, the larger model is worth the space. The app tells you which one it recommends and why.

What it asks your phone for, and why. The internet, only to download a model, a voice or a content pack when you choose to, and to check what content packs are available when you open Discover. Whether you have a connection and whether it is metered, so a multi-gigabyte download never starts on mobile data without you saying so. A notification while a download is running, so it can carry on when you leave the app. The microphone, only when you use voice typing, which is transcribed on the phone. Your fingerprint or face, only if you turn on the app lock. That is the whole list.

Free and open source, under the AGPLv3.
